getRows.description: The rows that currently exist, by index.

canAppend.description: Whether `append()` would currently add a row, i.e. `maxItems` hasn't been reached.

canRemove.description: Whether `remove()` would currently remove a row, i.e. more than `minItems` remain.

append.description: Adds a row, if `maxItems` allows it.

remove.description: Removes the row at `index`, if `minItems` allows it.

id.description: The unique identifier of the field array.

name.description: The name the rows are nested under, e.g. `people` for `people[0][firstName]`.

itemCount.description: The number of rows the server rendered. It sets the state of the triggers before hydration, once the client runs it counts the rows in the DOM instead.

minItems.description: The fewest rows allowed. At this many, `remove()` and the remove triggers do nothing and the remove triggers are disabled.

maxItems.description: The most rows allowed. At this many, `append()` and the add trigger do nothing and the add trigger is disabled.

translations.description: The screen reader announcements of an added and a removed row. In a string, `%number%` is replaced with the 1-based position of the row, e.g. `Row %number% removed.`. A callback builds the message from the data of the row, and may use `%number%` in what it returns.

onItemAdded.type: ((detail: { index: number; componentNames: string[] }) => void) | undefined
onItemAdded.description: Called after a row was added by the add trigger, with its index and the client names of the components inside it, e.g. `['field', 'input']`. Call their `mountAll()` here: the field array doesn't know what the template of a row contains.

onItemRemoved.description: Called after a row was removed by its remove trigger, with the index it had. The later rows have already moved up by then.

RemoveTrigger.data-value: The index of the row the trigger removes.
